title: Extension Services and the Social Sustainability Mission of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs): A Critical Integrative Review
content: Higher education institutions (HEIs) are increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable development through research, instruction, and community engagement. However, contemporary higher education systems have become progressively research-oriented, prioritizing publication productivity, citation metrics, and institutional rankings. While these developments have expanded academic knowledge production, they have also contributed to a growing disconnect between knowledge generation and societal utilization. Within this context, extension services remain comparatively underprioritized despite their potential role in translating academic knowledge into meaningful community impact. This paper presents a critical integrative review of extension services in higher education, focusing on their conceptual evolution, institutional positioning, and contribution to the social sustainability mission of universities. The review examines how extension services have evolved from traditional technology-transfer and outreach models toward broader paradigms of community engagement, knowledge democratization, and sustainability-oriented development. It further analyzes the institutional marginalization of extension services within increasingly research-driven academic systems. Findings suggest that extension services remain insufficiently theorized and institutionally undervalued despite their critical role in promoting equitable knowledge access and community-centered development. The paper argues that extension services should be repositioned as central mechanisms through which HEIs translate academic knowledge into sustainable societal impact.
